_metadata.description: Validation-calibrated factors for the direct-jobs coefficient of land-based gaming, by property type.
_metadata.method: Geometric-mean ratio of the calculator's direct jobs coefficient to observed QCEW jobs per $1M of wages, by state and property type (2023, cells with at least 50 jobs). Model compensation is converted to QCEW-comparable wages by industry (QCEW private wages / BEA compensation: 0.698 for 713). factor = 1 / geometric-mean ratio. p05/p95 are the 5th and 95th percentiles of a lognormal fitted to 1/ratio across states, i.e. a 90% predictive interval for true direct jobs relative to the model coefficient.
_metadata.assumption: The benchmark identifies jobs per wage dollar. The factor corrects jobs and holds the compensation-per-output coefficient fixed.
_metadata.scope: Direct jobs only. Supplier and induced jobs have no observed benchmark and are not adjusted. Online operations are not covered. Bars/restaurants with slots (722410) are not calibrated: the only QCEW benchmark, NAICS 722410, covers all drinking places, not gaming taverns.
_metadata.outOfSampleCheck: A correction calibrated on 2023 removes the bias in 2024 (corrected ratio 1.00); calibrated on 2019 and applied to 2023 it overshoots by 13%. Re-estimate with each QCEW vintage.
_metadata.source: Philander, 'Multipliers for sectors that are not casinos' (Tourism Economics, under review); replication repository kphilander/casino-io-validation (commit 096a011), analysis_output/correction_factors.csv and correction_factors_tribal.csv (public on publication).
_metadata.tribal: tribalPropertyTypes are estimated the same way against tribal-government casinos (QCEW own_code 3). BEA records tribal gaming as a government enterprise, outside the private 713 industry the coefficients come from; tribal casinos sit close to the coefficient. Slot parlors are omitted for tribal properties (5 cells).
